steps.title: One table for all vector types
notes: Every vector type is one line of VECTOR_TYPES: key, BSID, default power and speed, scan order and preview colour. The table drives the parameter tree, the custom table, the sorting and the preview, so a new vector type needs only one new line here.
The bars on the left are the line energy P / v of these defaults.

lines: //          key                    bsid family               ds     P[W] v[mm/s] order color

steps.title: One parameter group per vector type
notes: The Scanning group is generated from the table: one child group grp_scan_<key> per vector type, created by create_scan_group with laser number, power, speed and focus.
That is why the dialog in the video shows fourteen sub-groups under Scanning, from First border to Solid support.

steps.title: Read the laser settings
notes: part.scanning is keyed by the BSID as a string, for example scanning['500'] for the volume hatch. read_scan returns laser number, power, speed and focus of one group.

lines: // One entry per vector type. Keys are bsids as strings (JSON compatible).
// speed: 1200, focus: 0 } (laser_index 1-based as in the UI).

steps.title: Every path carries its settings
notes: When a hatch is added to the layer, make_attr_info looks up the scan settings of its BSID, and EXPOSURE_ATTRIBUTES.apply writes power, speed and focus onto the paths. Changing the speed changes these attributes, not the geometry: in the video the toolpaths stay exactly the same.
Raising only the speed lowers the energy per volume: 1600 mm/s at 280 W gives 58 J/mm³ instead of 78 J/mm³.

lines: // The scan settings are stored with the BSID as string key, because

// Tip: The UI shows laser numbers starting at 1, the toolpath

steps.title: The custom table for the export
notes: build_custom_table stores the same settings once per BSID at the model, under the name customTable. The exporters and the host read it from there; laserIndex is 0-based, laserNumber 1-based like in the dialog.

With laser assignment switched on, the table gets one more entry per vector type and laser (for example 2500 = volume hatch on laser 3). After the post-processing, store_reduced_custom_tables keeps only the BSIDs the paths really use, always starting from the full copy.

steps.title: The exposure time estimate
notes: After sorting, estimate_layer_time_ms walks every path of the layer in its final order. For each path add_path_time adds exposed length ÷ speed of the path, the jumps at the jump speed, the jump delays and the mark delays (see Laser timing).

The post-processing sums all layers into built_time_estimation_ms; the export writes it to export_info.json. For the hatch plate the volume hatch is about 10 400 mm per layer, so 1200 → 1600 mm/s saves about 217 s: 0:14:54 → 0:11:18 in the video.

lines: // Only the total skip length is known, not every single jump, so
// the delay is taken for the mean jump length. This is exact while
// all jumps are shorter than the length limit (the delay is linear
// there) or the scaling is off; otherwise it is a slight
// overestimate. Reading every jump would cost far more time.

recipes.title: A faster volume hatch by default
recipes.why: Shorter build times, as in the video.
recipes.result: New profiles start with 1600 mm/s for the volume hatch. On the hatch plate the estimate in export_info.json drops by about 3.6 minutes, from 0:14:54 to 0:11:17. Check the energy in the Energy view: you may have to raise the power as well.

recipes.title: Faster, with the same energy per volume
recipes.why: Save time without lowering the energy density.
recipes.result: 373 W at 1600 mm/s gives the same 78 J/mm³ as 280 W at 1200 mm/s. Whether the melt pool behaves the same must still be tested on the machine.

recipes.title: Supports on a second laser
recipes.why: On a machine with two lasers, the supports can run in parallel with the part.
recipes.result: Wall and solid supports default to laser 2 (laserIndex 1 in the custom table). The time estimate gives every laser its own clock, so a layer takes as long as the slower of part and supports. With laser assignment switched on, the scan fields decide instead.

edits.before: scan_defaults: { laser_index: 1, power: a_power, speed: a_speed, focus: 0.0 },
edits.after: scan_defaults: { laser_index: (a_bsid >= 700) ? 2 : 1, power: a_power, speed: a_speed, focus: 0.0 },
